title: Copying a value
summary: Change one name and see what happens to the other.
analogy: Write a number on two sticky notes. Replacing the number on one note leaves the other note as it was.

explanations.explorer: Python gives each name a value to point to. Make two names point to the same number. Then change the first name and check the second.
explanations.builder: Assignment connects a name to an object. When you assign a new integer to original, Python updates that one name. copied still refers to the earlier integer.
explanations.pro: The diagram shows name bindings, not integer object identity. Rebinding one name leaves the other binding intact. Mutable objects introduce a separate case: an in-place change can be visible through every alias.

remember: The right side is read first.
Assignment sets the name on the left.
Two names can refer to the same number.
commonMistake: Reading copied = original as a rule that keeps the names in sync. It runs once, using the value original has at that moment.

challenges.prompt: A points to 7. B is assigned A. A is then assigned 2. What will print(B) show?
challenges.hint: Trace B back to the moment when it was assigned.
challenges.explanation: B was assigned when A referred to 7, so B still refers to 7.

challenges.prompt: Fill the blank to assign the value 3 to score: score ___ 3.
challenges.explanation: A single equals sign assigns the number on its right to the name on its left.

challenges.prompt: You set score = 5. Which line prints that exact name?
challenges.explanation: Only score matches the name from the assignment.

challenges.prompt: Arrange the lines so saved keeps 3 and score changes to 9 before the print.
challenges.hint: Save the original value before changing score.
challenges.explanation: The copy uses the value of score at that moment. After score is rebound, saved still points to 3.

challenges.prompt: After a = 10 and b = a, which statement leaves b unchanged?
challenges.hint: Find the statement that assigns only a.
challenges.explanation: a = 99 rebinds a. Both other options assign a new integer to b.

flashcards.back: A connection between a name and the object it currently refers to.

flashcards.front: Which side of an assignment is evaluated first?
flashcards.back: The right side is evaluated, and its result is assigned to the target on the left.

flashcards.front: What does it mean to rebind a name?
flashcards.back: It means assigning a new object to a name that already had a binding.

flashcards.front: Are score and Score the same Python name?
flashcards.back: They are different names. Python distinguishes uppercase and lowercase letters.
